headline: Ratchet & Clank builds NTSC-U in its own tree and carries over existing C
summary: NTSC-U now builds within this repository instead of requiring the NTSC decompilation as a submodule (#121). Carrying existing definitions from PAL v1.00 and NTSC-J takes NTSC-U from 74.21% to 76.10% matched code and from 4,756 to 4,822 of 5,097 functions (#122). A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. PAL v2.00 remains at 98.48% matched code and 5,089 of 5,120 functions, and the pull requests describe no newly written C.
highlights: All 20 NTSC-U programs reproduce the original bytes. Upstream NTSC names are still read at a pinned revision, without making recursive clones carry its whole tree (#121).
A newer NTSC naming batch is adopted, and provenance comments are corrected to credit the upstream decompilation as GPL-3.0 (#123, #124).
